$$
B={[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5\end{aligned}]},\,[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -3\end{aligned}]

Consider the basis $B$ of ${R}^{2}$ (shown above) and a basis $C$ of ${R}^{3}.$
The matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the linear map $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{3}$ relative to these bases, and the vector $x\in {R}^{2},$ are also given. Find $[T(x)]_{C}.$

activity_context.topic_title: The Matrix of a Linear Map Relative to Two Bases

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Image of a Vector Given With Respect to the Standard Basis Under a Linear Map
examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14067114/assets/8caf13cdbf21ddfb1a121ede6ec0c21da155065905547bbd86b0e52cd57141da.png)

Consider the basis $\mathcal{B}$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$ (shown above) and a basis $\mathcal{C}$ of $\mathbb{R}^3.$
The matrix $[\mathbf{T}]_{\mathcal{B}|\mathcal{C}}$ of the linear map $\mathbf{T}:\mathbb{R}^2 \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^3$ relative to these bases, and the vector $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^2,$ are also given. Find $[\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{x})]_{\mathcal{C}}.$
examples.worked_solution:
We can find the coordinates of the image of $\mathbf{x}$ under $\mathbf{T}$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{C}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to find $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}},$ the coordinates of $\mathbf{x}$ relative to $\mathcal{B}.$ So, let

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14067114/assets/a5b6f5f41dffd99a885bb872eac6f1e6a24bd604b360256194a0bf16b32ef381.png)

This gives us the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=5 \\ 4{x}_{1}-5{x}_{2}=2.\end{aligned}
$$

We now row-reduce the corresponding augmented matrix using Gaussian elimination, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 5 \\ 4 & -5 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-4){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & 3 & -18\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -6\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -7 \\ 0 & 1 & -6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14067114/assets/862742d57ad0ae4b56d6f345d825313bebf0d712f9c59ea1ed8b55d0a2eea22e.png)

Finally, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}17 \\ -9 \\ -6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
$$
[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & -5 \\ -1 & 0 & -9\end{aligned}],\,[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]
$$

Suppose $B$ and $C$ are bases of the vector spaces $V$ and $W,$ respectively. The matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the linear map $T:V\to W$ relative to these bases, and the coordinates of the vector $x\in V$ relative to $B$ are shown above. Find $[T(x)]_{C}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The coordinates of the image of $x$ under $T$ relative to the basis $C$ can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & -5 \\ -1 & 0 & -9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 21\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
